Issued at 252 AM EDT Wed Sep 30 2026

Today-Tonight... Upper level trough over the eastern seaboard will 
push offshore. A surface high pressure in the western Atlantic will 
slowly shift northward, with the axis continuing to build over the 
Florida peninsula. Locally, onshore (east to southeast) winds will 
remain in place, with speeds generally 5-10 mph. The east coast sea 
breeze will form each afternoon, enhancing the winds to around 10 
mph behind the sea breeze. Moisture will continue to increase, with 
forecast PW values rising to 1.7-2.2" this afternoon, with the 
highest values occurring around Lake Okeechobee and the Treasure 
Coast. This will support increasing rain and storm chances today, 
with a low to medium (20-50 percent) chance of rain. Isolated to 
scattered onshore moving showers will be possible along the coast 
through the morning hours before coverage increases to widely 
scattered and shifts across all of east central Florida this 
afternoon. Lightning storm activity will also increase this 
afternoon. Greatest coverage of showers and storms will be across 
the Treasure Coast and around Lake Okeechobee this afternoon. 
Isolated to scattered showers will once again be possible along the 
coast through tonight. Main storm hazards will be frequent lightning 
strikes, gusty winds up to 45 mph, and locally heavy downpours. 

Temperatures will continue a slight warming trend today, with 
afternoon highs forecast to be in the mid to upper 80s along the 
coast, and upper 80s to near 90 degrees across the interior. Peak 
heat indices will be in the low to mid 90s. Warm and muggy 
conditions anticipated for tonight, with lows in the low to mid 70s.  

Thursday-Friday... An upper high pressure over the western Atlantic 
will shift westward, towards the Florida peninsula, through late 
week. At the surface, high pressure off the Carolina coast will 
remain in place through late week, with the axis continuing to 
build over the Florida peninsula. Locally, east to southeast winds 
will dominate, becoming enhanced (around 10-15 mph) each afternoon 
with the formation of the east coast sea breeze. Moisture increases 
over the area through the period, with forecast PW values raising to 
2.0-2.3" Thursday afternoon and 2.2-2.6" on Friday afternoon. This 
will result in increasing rain and storm chances through the period. 
Isolated to scattered onshore moving showers will continue to be 
possible along the coast through the overnight hours and into each 
morning, with coverage increasing to scattered to numerous and 
shifting across all of east central Florida each afternoon. There is 
a medium (40-60 percent) chance of rain on Thursday, and a medium to 
high (50-70 percent) chance of rain on Friday. Greatest potential 
for storms will be across the interior, west of I-95, each 
afternoon. Main storm hazards will be frequent lightning strikes, 
gusty winds, and locally heavy downpours. A few stronger storms may 
be possible, however due to the warming mid level temps and 
saturated airmass, the potential for stronger storms is limited.

A slight warming trend will continue, with warm and humid conditions 
forecast. Afternoon highs will be in the upper 80s to low 90s with 
peak heat indices reaching 98-103 degrees. Overnight lows will be 
warm and muggy with lows in the low to mid 70s.  

Saturday-Tuesday... An upper level ridge will build over the Florida 
peninsula this weekend and will remain in place through early next 
week. At the surface, a cold front will move into the Deep South 
this weekend before shifting southward into northern Florida early 
next week and into north-central Florida on Tuesday. Locally, east 
to southeast winds at 5-10 mph will dominate through Monday, before 
winds become east to northeast and increase to 10-15 mph on Tuesday 
as the cold front moves through the area. Deep moisture will shift 
north and west of the region this weekend, which will lead to a 
gradual decrease in shower and storm chances Saturday and Sunday.
Moisture will then increase over the area into next week as the 
front approaches and pushes through, resulting in rain and storm 
chances rising into early next week. However, scattered to numerous 
showers and storms are forecast each day, with a few stronger storms 
remaining possible. Temperatures will continue to be slightly above 
normal for this time of year with afternoon highs in the upper 80s 
to low 90s. Overnight lows will be warm with lows in the low to mid 
70s.
